results.title: Human-AI Relationships and Their Therapeutic Implications
results.reason: The paper examines human-AI relationships and their clinical implications for therapists, directly addressing how clinicians should understand, assess, and ethically navigate AI companion relationships in therapeutic practice.
results.authors: Ciarán O'Driscoll; Bettina Moltrecht; Martin Dechant

results.title: An Empirically Informed Cognitive‑Behavioral Formulation of Obsessional Jealousy
results.reason: The paper directly addresses a clinically significant condition (obsessional jealousy) with clear implications for psychological assessment and treatment development, fitting within the clinical psychology practice relevance criteria.
results.authors: Sigrid Elfström; Johanna Linde; Johan Bjureberg; Josef Isung; Anna Norberg; David Mataix-Cols; Johan Ahlen

results.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of psychological therapy in prehabilitation pathway
results.reason: The paper evaluates psychological therapy in cancer prehabilitation, which is directly relevant to clinical psychology practice. It addresses mental health interventions for cancer patients, a population with significant psychological distress, and examines the clinical utility of embedded psychological support in improving both mental health and functional outcomes.
results.authors: Paulina Hunt; Melissa Covington; Nima Golijani-Moghaddam; Kate Maguire; Dr Sam Malins; James Rathbone; Rebecca Wynn; Sophie Leighton; Catherine Macauley; Maisie Cropley

results.title: Reconstructing Identity after Conversion Practices:  An Interpretative Phenomeno
results.reason: This study directly addresses clinical psychology practice by examining the psychological impacts of conversion practices on gay men and their identity reconstruction processes, which has clear implications for therapeutic practice with LGBTQ+ populations.
